payload.report: 49-year-old male with acute symmetric proximal weakness, sensory tingling/pain, and lower-limb hyporeflexia without upper motor neuron signs. Normal NCS broadened the differential, but needle EMG showing abnormal spontaneous activity and neurogenic recruitment is pivotal: it refutes acquired myopathy and NMJ disorder, supporting a peripheral neurogenic process. These clinical features and hyporeflexia favor Guillain-Barré syndrome; expert consensus raises GBS to 0.65 as the leading diagnosis. Myopathy remains possible at 0.2, NMJ disorder is unlikely at 0.1. Thus the diagnosis is Guillain-Barré syndrome.
